newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares end off as profit-taking kicks in.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares end off as profit-taking kicks in.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange fell in steady profit-taking as investors grew concerned about share valuations, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share .IBC index fell 2.80 percent to 9,254.84, as 35 stocks fell, four rose and six closed flat.
Brokers said profit-taking would likely continue for the rest of the week as prices adjust after a prolonged rally that has set successive highs in recent sessions.
"I think the market still has room for growth, although more slowly," said Intervalores broker Ricardo Marino.
The much-expected bout of taking was across-the-board, but was not panic, brokers said. "The market has support. Every time it falls, there is demand again," Marino said.
Trade was moderate at 8.218 billion bolivars ($16.8 million).

Among leading stocks, bellwether Electricidad de Caracas slipped 23.00 bolivars to 802.00 bolivars, telephone company CANTV fell 215.00 bolivars to 3,000.00 bolivars, while cement company Vencemos class 1 stock fell 21.00 bolivars to 1064.00 bolivars and class 2 stock fell 20.00 bolivars to 950.00 bolivars.
